svg.font-family: Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: How nightshift works
svg.desc: An investigation starts from a trigger: an alert fires, you ask a question with Investigate on the home page, you mention @Elastic in Slack, an automation runs on an alert or a schedule, or Detection finds a significant event. Detection is its own engine: it watches your logs and learns Knowledge Indicators about your services, infrastructure, and dependencies. Knowledge Indicators become rules, and the rules raise significant events. The investigation queries your logs, metrics, and traces, reads code in a temporary sandbox when GitHub is connected, and tests several hypotheses, confirming or dismissing each one with a confidence level. Before it starts, it reads the Wiki and Memory; when it ends, it writes back what it learned, so each investigation improves the next. The result is a likely cause, the evidence, and proposed actions. You decide whether to apply or decline each action; nightshift does not change your systems.
